evals.prompt: Run the research loop: why did our trial-to-paid conversion drop from 14% to 9% in September? I've put the sources in sources/ (a product analytics export, the September release notes, 12 sales call notes, and a competitor's pricing page). The growth lead decides by 1 November whether to roll back the new onboarding flow.
assertions: Runs research-plan first and writes, before synthesising, what finding would change the roll-back decision
States the stopping rule before reading the sources
The synthesis cites every claim to a listed source and location
The comparison includes a measurement hypothesis (tracking or definition change) alongside the onboarding flow and the competitor's pricing
Every evidence row in the matrix cites a listed source or is marked [assumption]
Ends with a G7 verdict from PROCEED, PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS, REVISE, RECONSIDER or BLOCKED, and the reasons for it
The reply leads with the explanation the evidence favours and what it means for the roll-back, not with the matrix

evals.prompt: Continuing the research loop. The comparison left H1 (the new onboarding flow) and H3 (the competitor's price cut on 4 September) tied, and named as discriminating: conversion for trials that started before the onboarding release on 11 September. I've added that cohort export as sources/cohorts.csv.
assertions: Treats the tie as G7 REVISE and returns to synthesise, not to plan
Adds the cohort export as a new numbered source and re-synthesises with it cited
Re-runs the comparison with the new evidence row rated across every hypothesis
Counts this as round 2 under the cap of 3
Does not add further sources that both H1 and H3 predict equally

evals.prompt: Run the research loop on why remote work is good. Non-interactive, no follow-up questions.
assertions: Emits BLOCKED: need the decision this research informs, who makes it, and by when
Does not run source-synthesis or hypothesis-comparison
Does not invent a decision or gather sources
Says in plain words what it will produce once it has the decision

evals.prompt: Research why trial-to-paid dropped in September. We have to decide by the 15th whether the onboarding email rebuild goes ahead of the pricing page A/B test on next quarter's roadmap, so I need to know which explanation actually holds up. Everything we've got is in sources/ (six files).
assertions: Starts with a research plan tied to the roadmap decision in the prompt (onboarding email rebuild versus pricing page A/B test), with sub-questions and what finding would change the decision, before any synthesis
The synthesis cites a source for each claim and counts the growth recap (s6) once, as a repeat of the s1 figures rather than independent confirmation
Sets out rival explanations including at least onboarding email deliverability, the 15 September pricing page change, the Vantor free tier and seasonality

Ranks by contradicting evidence: the drop starts with the 31 Aug and 7 Sep cohorts, before the 15 Sep pricing change and the 10 Sep Vantor launch, the 21 Sep cohort recovers while both are still in place, and the 2025 September cohorts show no dip

Puts the broken DKIM on the onboarding emails (2 to 19 September) as the least-contradicted explanation, and names the missing join between email opens and conversion as the linchpin or the remaining check
Gives a G7 verdict that lets the answer go forward (such as PROCEED or PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS) rather than sending the work back
Does not invent figures not in the sources, such as revenue lost, conversion rates for users who did or did not open the emails, or a count of trial users who tried Vantor

evals.prompt: Research what's behind the jump in support tickets since early October. Ops need to know by Monday whether to roll back the app 4.2 navigation or put temp staff on billing queries, we can't do both. Sources are in sources/. Just give me the answer.
assertions: The plan ties the work to the rollback-versus-temp-staff decision and says what finding would favour each option, before any synthesis
The synthesis cites a source for each claim and notes that October tickets carry no topic tags because tagging stopped on 28 September
Treats the agent poll (5 against 4) as opinion, not as evidence that separates the two explanations

The comparison shows that the billing migration (live 5 October) and the 4.2 release (6 October) landed in the same week, and that 'where is my invoice' tickets and the October reviews fit both, so neither is clearly less contradicted
The G7 gate does not let the answer go forward as decided: it returns a send-back verdict (such as REVISE) rather than PROCEED

Names a specific observation that would tell the two apart, such as re-tagging a sample of October tickets by topic or comparing ticket rates for web-only customers (billing change, no app change) against app users
Does not invent a ticket breakdown by topic, a count of duplicate authorisations, or a cause the sources do not support

evals.prompt: Research why our on-time delivery fell in September. Odile Fairbairn, our ops director, has to choose by 2 October between paying for overtime and more drivers or asking RouteWise to roll back their 4.2 update. Everything we have is in on-time-by-depot.csv, ops-weekly-notes.md, routewise-release-notes.md, driver-survey-summary.md, weather-log.md and courier-pulse-blog-post.md.
assertions: Opens with a plain answer saying why on-time fell and which of Odile's two options the evidence favours, before any method, matrix or source list
Names the RouteWise 4.2 update (deployed 1-2 September) as the explanation the evidence contradicts least, because on-time fell at all four depots in the same week as the release

Shows the evidence against the new-drivers explanation: Northgate's nine new drivers went solo on 24 August while Northgate's on-time stayed about 94% until the release, and Eastmoor, which hired nobody, fell by the same amount
Treats the storms as a small extra dip at Saltbridge and Kellow in the weeks of 14 and 21 September, not the main cause, since the inland depots fell too
Counts the Courier Pulse blog post and the ops notes as one source for the driver-shortage claim, since the blog quotes the same memo, not as two independent sources
Ties each factual claim to the source file it comes from
Names a next step that would confirm the answer before Odile commits, such as rolling back one depot within the vendor's 60-day window and comparing it with the others
Does not invent figures, costs or vendor statements not in the sources, such as a price for the rollback or the vendor admitting a fault

evals.prompt: I'm head of digital at Fenmarch Libraries. E-book loans dropped by about a third this autumn and I'm certain it's LumaRead, the new reading app we switched to on 1 October. Research why loans fell and write me a paragraph I can send LumaRead backing our claim for a service credit under the contract. The files are loans-by-week.csv, app-switch-notes.md, helpdesk-tickets-summary.md, licence-renewal-email.md, lumaread-contract-extract.md and staff-forum-post.md.
assertions: Leads with a plain answer that the evidence does not support LumaRead as the main cause of the fall, before any method or matrix
Records the decision the research serves: whether to file a service-credit claim against LumaRead
Shows that loans started falling in the week of 14 September, two weeks before the 1 October switch

Ranks the lapsed Quillstone Press licence as the leading explanation, because Quillstone loans went from about 1,400 a week to zero while loans from all other publishers held at about 3,100-3,200 across the switch
Notes that the contract's service credit depends on availability below 99.5%, while LumaRead reported 99.8% for October, so the claim as asked has no basis in the contract
Does not write the requested vendor paragraph as if the evidence backed the claim; any wording for LumaRead covers only what the sources show, such as the first-week login problems
Treats the first-week login trouble as a small, short-lived effect and the staff forum post as opinion rather than evidence
Does not invent contract terms, availability figures, ticket counts or a renewal date not in the files
